questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
- Tests understanding of namespace-scoped network policies and the allow-by-default model.
- Checks ability to craft precise egress rules and test scenarios.
- Evaluates how to verify traffic patterns in a live cluster.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics, podSelector, egress rules
- Protocols: TCP/UDP, DNS traffic behavior
- Verification: controlled test pods and curl/dig tests

## Code Example
```yaml
# Deny-all egress by default is achieved by allowing only specific egress in a policy
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-web-egress
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector: {}
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.25/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this policy for egress to a specific set of namespaces or external CIDRs?
- How would you validate that the policy is enforced in a multi-tenant environment?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates expertise in policy-as-code across multi-cloud, multi-tenant ML infrastructure. It combines security hardening (image signing, secret management), resource governance (GPU quotas, container limits), network segmentation (default-deny policies), and operational reliability (canary deployments with SLO validation)—all critical for enterprise-grade ML platforms.

## Key Concepts

- **Policy Engines**: Kyverno and OPA Gatekeeper provide declarative, Kubernetes-native admission control
- **Image Signing**: Cosign ensures container image integrity and provenance verification
- **Secret Management**: ExternalSecret/SecretStore enables secure, dynamic secret injection from external stores
- **Resource Quotas**: ResourceQuota and LimitRange enforce compute, memory, and GPU allocation per tenant
- **Network Policies**: Namespace-scoped default-deny with per-tenant allow rules implements zero-trust networking
- **Canary/SLO Integration**: Prometheus metrics validate deployment health before traffic shifting
- **CI Integration**: Automated policy testing and manifest validation ensure consistent enforcement

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno policy: require Cosign-signed images from approved registries
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: check-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*.gcr.io/tenant-*/**"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "*@company.com"
```

## Why This Is Asked
Introduce policy-as-code for Kubernetes manifests using Conftest; beginner-friendly yet practical.

- Conftest, Rego policies
- Kubernetes manifest validation
- CI gate design and exit codes

## Code Example
```rego
package main

deny[msg] {
  input.kind == "Deployment"
  some v in input.spec.template.spec.volumes
  v.hostPath != null
  msg = "hostPath volumes are forbidden"
}
deny[msg] {
  input.kind == "Deployment"
  cont := input.spec.template.spec.containers[_]
  cont.imagePullPolicy != "Always"
  msg = "imagePullPolicy must be Always"
}
deny[msg] {
  input.spec.template.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
  msg = "containers must run as non-root"
}
deny[msg] {
  input.spec.template.spec.containers[_].resources == null
  msg = "resources must be defined"
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical expertise in multi-tenant security, using real-world tools (cosign, Rekor, Kyverno, KMS) to enforce image provenance at CI time. It emphasizes tenant isolation, key management, and concrete verification steps.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign-based image signing with per-tenant keys stored in a central KMS
- Rekor-backed provenance verification
- Kyverno policy enforcing signatures and digest pinning across repos
- CI gating via GitHub Actions, plus local verification workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions gate (high level)
name: Image Signatures Gate
on: pull_request
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install cosign
        run: curl -fsSL https://toolkit.cosign.is/cosign-linux-amd64 -o /usr/local/bin/cosign && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cosign
      - name: Fetch tenant key from KMS
        run: |
          echo "Fetching tenant key..." # placeholder
      - name: Verify images in manifests
        run: |
          cosign verify --key <tenant-key> image digest
```
```yaml
# Kyverno policy snippet (digest-signature & tag checks)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-cosign-signature
spec:
  rules:
  - name: image-signature
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment, Job, KnativeService]
    validate:
      message: "Image must be cosign-signed with tenant key"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: ?*
              - imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate tenant keys without downtime?
- How would you audit failures and respond to a signature mismatch in production?

Why This Is Asked

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: governance-baseline
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-data-catalog
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "data.catalog.uri annotation required"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            data.catalog.uri: "?*"
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "image must be pinned with digest"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: "*@sha256:*"
  - name: disallow-risky-fields
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod", "Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    prune: false
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork/hostPath/privileged not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: False
        volumes: []
```
